edges.mechanism: Potent CYP1A2 (and CYP2C19) inhibition blocks melatonin 6-hydroxylation; melatonin AUC up 17-fold and Cmax up 12-fold. SmPC says avoid the combination.
edges.evidence: Human PK study plus microsome data plus regulatory label; high certainty for PK effect

edges.with: CYP1A2 inhibitors (ciprofloxacin/quinolones, cimetidine, oestrogens/oral contraceptives, methoxypsoralens)
edges.mechanism: Inhibit CYP1A2-mediated melatonin clearance, raising exposure and next-day sedation risk.
edges.evidence: In vitro (5-methoxypsoralen), PK review (oral contraceptives), SmPC listing

edges.mechanism: Induction of CYP1A2 may lower melatonin levels and efficacy.
edges.evidence: Regulatory label statement; mechanistic

edges.mechanism: Caffeine competes for or inhibits CYP1A2; 600 mg raised oral melatonin Cmax 142% and AUC 120%, more in non-smokers and CYP1A2*1F/*1F carriers. Caffeine is also arousing, which pharmacodynamically opposes melatonin's sleep effect.
edges.evidence: Human PK crossover (n=12) and phenotyping study

edges.mechanism: Additive pharmacodynamic CNS depression via GABA-A: PR-melatonin plus zolpidem worsened psychomotor, driving and memory performance with no PK change. Melatonin does not aid benzodiazepine discontinuation.
edges.evidence: Randomized crossover RCT; SmPC; MA of 6 RCTs

edges.mechanism: Case reports of harm (bleeding or INR change) in warfarin users; melatonin lowers FVIII:C and fibrinogen; listed among supplements associated with bleeding in anticoagulated patients.
edges.evidence: Case reports cited in Cochrane review; small RCT on coagulation factors; narrative review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Evening melatonin 5 mg raised 24-h SBP by 6.5 and DBP by 4.9 mmHg and heart rate by 3.9 bpm in patients controlled on nifedipine GITS; proposed competition with calcium-channel blockade.
edges.evidence: Double-blind crossover RCT (n=47); systematic review notes antihypertensive interactions

edges.mechanism: Melatonin modulates T-cell activation and differentiation, partly via calcineurin, and could theoretically counteract immunosuppression; SmPC advises against use in autoimmune disease for lack of data.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic review plus regulatory precaution; no clinical interaction data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both converge on mTOR/SIRT1 signalling; melatonin enhanced rapamycin's AKT/mTOR suppression and anticancer effect while reducing toxicity to normal cells in preclinical models. Any immunological interaction in humans is unknown.
edges.evidence: Preclinical only (cell and xenograft); mechanistic review

edges.mechanism: Melatonin can impair glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity (10 mg/d for 3 months reduced insulin sensitivity 12% in T2D), especially near meals and in MTNR1B risk carriers; one MA reports improved FBG/HbA1c, so the net effect is uncertain.
edges.evidence: Crossover RCTs and MA with conflicting results; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Combined melatonin-magnesium-zinc supplement improved PSQI by 6.8 points vs placebo in elderly insomniacs; the effect is additive and not separated by component.
edges.evidence: Single double-blind RCT (n=43) of combination product

edges.mechanism: Both improved insomnia vs placebo in cancer patients (melatonin more than theanine); a complementary sleep-promoting mechanism is plausible, but the combination is untested.
edges.evidence: Single three-arm RCT without combination arm; very low certainty for synergy

edges.mechanism: Glycine improves subjective sleep or fatigue via SCN neuropeptides without changing plasma melatonin; additive sleep effects are plausible, with no PK interaction expected.
edges.evidence: Human plus rodent study of glycine alone; no combination data

edges.mechanism: Smoking induces CYP1A2: exogenous melatonin AUC was about 3-fold lower while smoking than after abstinence; quitting can sharply raise melatonin exposure.
edges.evidence: Human PK study; PK systematic review

edges.mechanism: CYP1A2 genotype alters melatonin exposure and the size of caffeine-melatonin interaction (larger in *1F/*1F).
edges.evidence: Small human PK/phenotyping studies

edges.mechanism: Melatonin worsens glucose tolerance (11.7%) and suppresses first-phase beta-cell responsivity (40%) only in risk-allele carriers; effect on glucose AUC 6-fold larger in carriers when taken in the morning.
edges.evidence: Randomized crossover trials (2015, 2026 Diabetes Care)

edges.mechanism: Evening alcohol suppresses endogenous melatonin 15-19% and adds sedation; SmPC says alcohol reduces Circadin's effectiveness on sleep.
edges.evidence: Controlled lab study; regulatory label

edges.mechanism: Avoid dosing close to meals; possible deterioration of glycemia, particularly in MTNR1B carriers and at 10 mg/d.
edges.evidence: RCTs with conflicting MA; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Case reports suggest possible harm in epilepsy and one pediatric MA case of mild generalized epilepsy; controlled trials show no worsening, and possibly better seizure severity and sleep latency.
edges.evidence: Cochrane (inconclusive), MA of 10 RCTs, case reports; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Immunomodulatory T-cell effects; regulatory label does not recommend use for lack of data.
edges.evidence: Regulatory precaution; mechanistic

edges.mechanism: No insomnia RCTs in pregnancy; melatonin likely passes into milk. SmPC does not recommend use, although trials for other indications reported no major safety signals.
edges.evidence: Scoping review of human studies; regulatory label

edges.mechanism: Gummy formulations with label content up to 347% (US gummies) and 0-667% (children's products) of declared dose drive a surge in pediatric ingestions: +530% in 2012-2021 with 2 deaths, and about 10,930 ED visits in 2019-2022.
edges.evidence: National poison-center and ED surveillance; product content surveys

edges.mechanism: Unpublished AHA 2025 abstract: long-term melatonin use in insomnia associated with incident HF (HR 1.89) and mortality; confounding by insomnia severity likely. NHANES reanalysis found no significant association, and RCTs in cardiac patients show no harm.
edges.evidence: Observational abstract (not peer reviewed) plus counter-analyses; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Not an assay artifact: melatonin taken shortly before a glucose load physiologically worsens glucose tolerance, especially in MTNR1B carriers, which could bias OGTT results.
edges.evidence: Randomized crossover trials
